title: The comparison: the two main estimates

headline.label: BSZ main estimate and JR main estimate, on the common output (b)
headline.definition: the two analyses' own main estimates, next to each other: BSZ's net total (wealth tax + extra income tax from selling assets - income tax lost to leavers, present value of 5 years) and JR's NBER September 2026 mean NPV (perpetuity). Under the common output (b), the net fiscal effect, they are the bridge's two ends, $106.8B and −$39.0B (the exact expectation of the Monte Carlo whose seeded run is −$38.886B); the gap between the ends, $145.8B, is stated in the bridge

verified_by: Rscript, layer 6 at eee3493: score_common(bridge_inputs(read_contracts())$sup)[['b']] = 106.796 and rauh_nber_expectation(0, 72, 0.30, 0.60, 3.3, 5.8, 0.015, 0.045)[['b']] = -38.980; the same from export/r/ends.csv (bsz_model, nber_own on (b)), from export/py/ends.csv, and from the headline and the end bars in assets/comparison-data.js. The JR main estimate as shown, −$38.886B, is the JR contract row npv_mc_nber_mean (the authors' seeded run), traced by the JR chain
runs_for_a_stranger: AUDIT.md step 8, level 2: .github/workflows/comparison-ci.yml rebuilds the comparison in R and Python on a clean runner; no one-click (Binder) yet.

invisible(lapply(list.files("comparison/R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE), source))   # every function on the chain

layers.name: The numbers on the explorer
layers.what: This layer is the explorer's own JavaScript, not R or Python; the R and Python code starts at layer 3. The page loads the bridge's data file and prints the two main estimates from its headline object: headline.bsz, the BSZ net total, and headline.rjkdc, the JR NBER mean NPV as the JR pipeline reproduces the authors' seeded run. The two-bar chart below them takes the first and last bars of the current view (endsOf); in the default view, output (b) at each analysis's own horizon, these are the bridge's two ends. The BSZ end is the same number as the BSZ main estimate; the JR end is the exact expectation of the same Monte Carlo, a little below the seeded run. The two panels below the header each list the disputed inputs with a five-position slider; the page reads every slider, builds the input vector with model.js (a JavaScript copy of score_common(), layer 6, checked against R by test-site.R) and draws the two bars. The static header carries the same two numbers, written by site.R (layer 3), so it reads the same with JavaScript off.
layers.inputs: D = window.__BRIDGE__ from assets/comparison-data.js (D.headline, D.sliders: the two input vectors and the revision constants); M = model.js

inputs_from.what: window.__BRIDGE__: the headline object and every bar of every view; the default view is series.own.b.shapley

layers.outputs: headline: '$106.8B' (BSZ main estimate) and '−$38.9B' (JR main estimate); bars: '$106.8B' (BSZ analysis) and '−$39.0B' (JR analysis)
layers.method_ref: Display only. The definitions are the method: BSZ's net total, wealth tax plus extra income tax from asset sales minus 5 years of lost income tax; JR's mean NPV in perpetuity. The footnote on the explorer says the common output (b) puts both on one definition, of which the two bars are the ends.

r.symbol: positions(), updatePanel(), drawBars(): read each panel's sliders, call model.js, draw the two bars

layers.name: The bridge's data file
layers.what: A generated JavaScript data file, not R or Python, written by R only (the Python twin writes the same numbers as CSV under comparison/export/py/). # The bars of every view of the bridge, in display order. The page shows each analysis in
# its latest version only: the first bar is the BSZ analysis (August 2026, Table 5 row 1),
# the last the JR analysis (Jaros and Rauh, NBER, September 2026). Between them: one
# step per disputed input (BSZ value to the JR value of its March 2026 version, the one
# whose inputs the common function takes one by one), the model difference, and the
# September 2026 revision. The
# export tables still carry the GGSS and March 2026 totals; the page shows neither as an end.
build_series <- function(ex, resid_label) {
  br <- ex$bridge; en <- ex$ends; steps <- bridge_steps()
  settings <- unique(en$horizon_setting)
  out <- list()
  for (st in settings) {
    Hlab <- if (st == "own") "" else {
      h <- sub("common_", "", st); if (h == "Inf") " (perpetuity)" else paste0(" (", h, "-year horizon)") }
    out[[st]] <- list()
    for (o in c("a", "b")) {
      e <- en[en$horizon_setting == st & en$output == o, ]
      out[[st]][[o]] <- list()
      for (m in c("shapley", "sequential")) {
        b <- br[br$horizon_setting == st & br$output == o, ]
        b <- if (m == "sequential") b[order(b$sequential_rank), ] else b[match(steps$step_id, b$step_id), ]
        keep <- abs(b$shapley) > 1e-12 | abs(b$sequential) > 1e-12
        b <- b[keep, ]
        L <- list()
        add <- function(id, type, value, label, kind = NULL)
          L[[length(L) + 1]] <<- list(id = id, type = type, value = value, label = label,
                                     short = unname(short_labels[id]), kind = kind)
        add("bsz", "total", e$bsz_model,
            if (o == "a") "BSZ analysis (August 2026): Table 5 row 1 wealth tax revenue"
            else paste0("BSZ analysis (August 2026): Table 5 row 1 net of its own extra income tax and lost income tax",

layers.name: The bridge's ends and steps
layers.what: build_all() estimates everything the pages show. For each horizon setting it estimates the model at the all-BSZ inputs (the BSZ end), runs the two decompositions of layer 5 for outputs (b) and (a), and computes the JR analysis's own expectations: its March 2026 version, where the disputed-input steps end, and the NBER September 2026 one, the JR end. Each ends row records the BSZ end, the model at the March 2026 inputs, that version's expectation, the model difference (rauh_residual), the NBER end (nber_own) and the September revision (nber_step).
layers.inputs: bi: the two input vectors; and the JR Monte Carlo ranges (wt_min/max, f_min/max, c_min/max, r_min/max)

inputs_from.what: the Shapley and one-order step values for each output and setting
score_common() at the all-BSZ inputs (v_sup) and rauh_nber_expectation() (own_n)
bi: sup and rauh, the two input vectors

layers.other_inputs: the horizon settings HORIZONS = 5, 10, 20, 30, 50 years and a perpetuity
layers.outputs: ends, own horizon, output (b): bsz_model 106.796, rauh_residual 0.099, nber_own -38.980, nber_step -14.273; gap = 106.796 - (-38.980) = 145.776
layers.method_ref: This OPA's reconciliation (PLAN.md, the common output; DISPUTES.md for each input). Checks: test-endpoints.R pins each end against the printed number; test-shapley.R that the steps sum to the gap; test-site.R that the steps, the model difference and the revision add up to the gap on (b).

  so <- k$bsz$outputs; oo <- k$rjkdc$outputs; d <- k$docs
  oi <- k$rjkdc$inputs
  steps <- bridge_steps()
  ids <- steps$step_id

  # ---- each analysis's own numbers ------------------------------------------------
  ggss_printed <- pick(so, "ggss_headline", "printed_value")
  bsz_row1     <- pick(so, "tab5_row1_wealth_tax_revenue")
  rauh_args <- list(wt_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_wt_min"),
                    wt_max = pick(oo, "revenue_confirmed6", "printed_value"),  # 67.51
                    baseline = pick(oo, "revenue_baseline", "printed_value"),  # 94.2
                    c_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min"), c_max = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max"),
                    r_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), r_max = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max"))

layers.name: Splitting the gap into steps
layers.what: Each step switches one disputed input from the BSZ value to the JR value of its March 2026 version, where the inputs are published. Because inputs interact, a step's size depends on when it is switched. shapley_bridge() averages each switch over every order, exactly: it estimates the model at all 2^11 = 2,048 subsets of switched inputs and weights each difference by how many orders produce it. sequential_bridge() switches them in one order, Hoopes's. Both sets of steps add up to the model gap between the two input vectors; the model difference and the September revision close the rest of the gap to the JR end.
layers.inputs: sup, rauh (the two input vectors) and the list of steps

inputs_from.what: score_common(): output (b) or (a) at any mix of the two input vectors
sup and rauh, the two input vectors

layers.other_inputs: step_inputs (which argument each step switches) and sequential_order()
layers.outputs: output (b), own horizon: eleven Shapley steps summing to -131.602; the largest are one_time_as_permanent -33.628, confirmed_departures -33.160, horizon -27.051; plus the model difference 0.099 and the September revision -14.273, together -145.776
layers.method_ref: Shapley value, the standard average-over-orders decomposition. test-shapley.R checks the sum in every setting and compares with a brute-force average over orders.

layers.name: The estimating function and the JR end
layers.what: score_common() is the one function that estimates both analyses. The wealth tax is 5% x base x (1 - real-estate share) x (1 - avoidance) x S, where S is the share of the base still taxed after departures and the mobility response. At the all-BSZ inputs S = 1, so the wealth tax is 0.05 x 2,307 x 0.9 = 103.815, BSZ Table 5 row 1; output (b) adds 3.682 of income tax from asset sales and subtracts 0.701, five years of lost income tax, giving 106.796, the BSZ end. rauh_nber_expectation() (model.R lines 134-138, bridge.py lines 156-160) is the JR end: with the revenue uniform on [0, 72], the departing share f on [0.30, 0.60], the income tax C on [3.3, 5.8] and r on [1.5%, 4.5%], all independent, the mean NPV is 36 - 0.45 x 4.55 x 36.620 = -38.980. This is the last layer that computes: its two outputs are the two ends.
layers.inputs: x: one input vector (sup at the BSZ end); the NBER Monte Carlo bounds

inputs_from.what: sup: tau 0.05, W_core 2157, W_noncit 150, re 0, alpha 0.10, d_conf 0, ...

layers.other_inputs: the NBER bounds wt_min = 0 (a literal in build.R), wt_max = 72 (contract row nber_ceiling_hardcoded), f, C and r ranges (contract rows nber_mc_f_*, rauh_mc_c_*, rauh_mc_r_*)
layers.method_ref: BSZ PDF p.24 (90% x 5% x $2,307B) and Table 5 row 1, p.39; Jaros and Rauh NBER c15504, the Monte Carlo in the authors' public repository (NPV_dist_v8.R). test-endpoints.R checks both ends against the printed numbers (the NBER one within Monte Carlo error of the printed -38.9).

r.snippet:
score_common <- function(x) {
  R0  <- x$tau * (x$W_core + x$W_noncit) * (1 - x$re)
  S   <- 1 - (x$d_conf + max(x$d_conf, x$eps * x$dtau)) / 2
  WT  <- R0 * (1 - x$alpha) * S
  X   <- WT * x$s * x$g * x$t_cg
  f   <- x$alpha * x$m + x$kappa * (1 - S) * (1 - x$alpha * x$m)
  A   <- expected_annuity(x$H, x$r_min, x$r_max)
  PV  <- f * x$C * A
  c(a = WT, b = WT + X - PV, R0 = R0, S = S, X = X, f = f, annual_loss = f * x$C,
    annuity = A, PV = PV)
}

layers.name: The two input vectors
layers.what: bridge_inputs() builds the two settings of every disputed input, each value read from a contract row or a transcribed document input. The BSZ base is the contract's 2,307 split into 150 of non-US-citizen residents and the rest; the JR values are those of its March 2026 version, from the JR contract's workbook sums and Monte Carlo ranges.
layers.inputs: k: the two contracts and the document inputs

inputs_from.what: k$bsz, k$rjkdc (inputs and outputs tables) and k$docs, looked up row by row with pick()

layers.outputs: sup: W_core 2157, W_noncit 150, alpha 0.10, re 0, d_conf 0, dtau 0, H 5, ...; rauh: W_core 1894.8, W_noncit 0, alpha 0, dtau 0.05, H Inf, ...
layers.method_ref: Each value's source and page is in comparison/export/r/inputs.csv (bridge_input_table()).

r.snippet:
bridge_inputs <- function(k) {
  si <- k$bsz$inputs; so <- k$bsz$outputs
  oi <- k$rjkdc$inputs;   oo <- k$rjkdc$outputs
  d  <- k$docs
  W0      <- pick(si, "baseline_net_worth")
  noncit  <- pick(d, "ggss_noncitizen_wealth")
  C_sup   <- pick(si, "ca_inctax_billionaires")
  kappa_s <- (pick(si, "leavers_annual_inctax") / pick(si, "leavers_wealth")) / (C_sup / W0)
  tau     <- pick(oi, "tax_rate")
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(tau, pick(si, "tax_rate"))))
  base_r  <- pick(oi, "baseline_net_worth")
  R0_r    <- pick(oo, "revenue_baseline")           # 94.304, the workbook's own sum
  conf6   <- pick(oo, "revenue_confirmed6")         # 67.511
  wt_min  <- pick(oi, "rauh_mc_wt_min")              # 35
  shared <- list(tau = tau, m = pick(si, "mobility_share"), g = pick(si, "gains_share"),
                 t_cg = pick(si, "ca_cg_rate"),
                 r_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), r_max = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max"))
  sup <- c(shared, list(
    W_noncit = noncit, W_core = W0 - noncit, re = 0, d_conf = 0,
    alpha = pick(si, "avoidance_rate"), dtau = 0, eps = pick(si, "semi_elasticity_permanent"),
    kappa = kappa_s, C = C_sup, H = pick(d, "bsz_loss_horizon"),
    s = pick(si, "sell_share")))
  rauh <- c(shared, list(
    W_noncit = 0, W_core = base_r, re = 1 - R0_r / (tau * base_r),
    d_conf = 1 - conf6 / R0_r, alpha = 0, dtau = tau,
    eps = (1 - wt_min / R0_r) / tau,
    kappa = 1, C = (pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min") + pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max")) / 2,
    H = pick(d, "rauh_loss_horizon"), s = 0))
  list(sup = sup, rauh = rauh)
}

def bridge_inputs(k):
    si, so = k["bsz"]["inputs"], k["bsz"]["outputs"]
    oi, oo = k["rjkdc"]["inputs"], k["rjkdc"]["outputs"]
    d = k["docs"]
    W0 = pick(si, "baseline_net_worth")
    noncit = pick(d, "ggss_noncitizen_wealth")
    C_sup = pick(si, "ca_inctax_billionaires")
    kappa_s = (pick(si, "leavers_annual_inctax") / pick(si, "leavers_wealth")) / (C_sup / W0)
    tau = pick(oi, "tax_rate")
    assert abs(tau - pick(si, "tax_rate")) < 1e-12
    base_r = pick(oi, "baseline_net_worth")
    R0_r = pick(oo, "revenue_baseline")
    conf6 = pick(oo, "revenue_confirmed6")
    wt_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_wt_min")
    shared = {"tau": tau, "m": pick(si, "mobility_share"), "g": pick(si, "gains_share"),
              "t_cg": pick(si, "ca_cg_rate"),
              "r_min": pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), "r_max": pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max")}
    sup = dict(shared, W_noncit=noncit, W_core=W0 - noncit, re=0.0, d_conf=0.0,
               alpha=pick(si, "avoidance_rate"), dtau=0.0,
               eps=pick(si, "semi_elasticity_permanent"), kappa=kappa_s, C=C_sup,
               H=pick(d, "bsz_loss_horizon"), s=pick(si, "sell_share"))
    rauh = dict(shared, W_noncit=0.0, W_core=base_r, re=1 - R0_r / (tau * base_r),
                d_conf=1 - conf6 / R0_r, alpha=0.0, dtau=tau, eps=(1 - wt_min / R0_r) / tau,
                kappa=1.0, C=(pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min") + pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max")) / 2,
                H=pick(d, "rauh_loss_horizon"), s=0.0)

layers.name: The raw source: the two export contracts
layers.what: The comparison reads exactly three kinds of file: each analysis's export contract (export/r/inputs.csv and outputs.csv, written by that analysis's own pipeline for others to read), the values transcribed from the PDFs with their page (comparison/data/document-inputs.csv) and Hoopes's digitized figure. pick() looks up one row and fails loudly if it is missing or duplicated. The chain stops here: what is behind each contract row is each analysis's own chain.
layers.outputs: for the two ends: BSZ baseline_net_worth 2307, avoidance_rate 0.1, tax_rate 0.05, tab5_row1 extra income tax and annual loss; JR nber_ceiling_hardcoded 72, nber_mc_f_min/max 0.30/0.60, rauh_mc_c_min/max 3.3/5.8, rauh_mc_r_min/max 0.015/0.045, npv_mc_nber_mean -38.886 (the JR main estimate); document input ggss_noncitizen_wealth 150

read_contracts <- function(root = comparison_root()) {
  side <- function(s) list(
    inputs  = read_csv_plain(file.path(root, s, "export", "r", "inputs.csv")),
    outputs = read_csv_plain(file.path(root, s, "export", "r", "outputs.csv")))
  docs <- read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "data", "document-inputs.csv"))
  docs$value <- as.numeric(docs$value)          # "Inf" parses to Inf
  list(bsz = side("bsz-analysis"),
       rjkdc = side("rjkdc-analysis"),
       docs       = docs,
       hoopes     = read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "data", "hoopes-fig2.csv")))
}

# Look up one value, failing loudly if the contract row is missing or duplicated.
pick <- function(df, id, col = "value", key = NULL) {
  key <- key %||% names(df)[1]
  hit <- df[df[[key]] == id, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(hit) != 1) stop(sprintf("expected exactly one row '%s', found %d", id, nrow(hit)))
  hit[[col]]
}
